candidateDeltaAudit.interfaceContract: NO INTERFACE CHANGE. No tool is added or removed, no input schema changes, and the exec payload keeps its exact closed key set (spec 267): outcome exited carries exitCode 0..255 with signal null, outcome signaled carries exitCode null with the signal name. The attempt-evidence JSONL, the provider materialization, the execution profile and every budget constant are untouched. What changes is text the model reads: the exec and shell tool descriptions.
candidateDeltaAudit.modelVisibleChanges: THREE STATEMENTS ARE ADDED, and this is the whole delta. (1) exec now says a process it starts directly reports its own end, so a signal-killed process returns outcome "signaled" with the signal name and exitCode null. (2) shell now says the shell reports its own exit status, so a command it ran that was killed surfaces as outcome "exited" with exitCode 128+N (139 for SIGSEGV, 137 for SIGKILL) and the signal name is not reported for that inner command. (3) Both say a program killed while running can lose output it had not flushed because output to a pipe is buffered, and to ask for unbuffered output (for example `python -u`) or the runtime's fault handler when a crash's own output matters.
candidateDeltaAudit.whyItem1IsNotACodeChange: The first requested item was to report a signal-terminated subprocess as a signal instead of exited. That already holds and is proven by packages/workspace-tools-backend/tests/backend.test.ts, which runs node under exec and asserts outcome "signaled", signal <SIGxxx>, exitCode null, with the pre-crash output kept. The largest-eigenval case looked like a violation because it used the shell tool: the harness supervises the shell, the shell's child died on SIGSEGV, and the shell itself exited normally with 139. The payload was therefore correct about the process it actually observed; what was missing was any statement of what 128+N means. That is why the fix is a stated rule rather than a different payload.
candidateDeltaAudit.reading: Against run 40823203153 this is a pure text delta of two tool descriptions. Only cells that debug a crashing native program can move, and largest-eigenval is the one cell where the missing fact was measured to cost the whole budget. Any other cell that moves is provider conditions or run variance, not this change.
